## Context / Problem

`rebar.opcert_service.jobs.run_job` starts dozens of child processes per job. On the macOS dev host each git start costs 0.11-0.33 s median and up to 1.3 s under load, about 95% of it outside git's own runtime (GIT_TRACE2: 25 `git --version` runs = 5.89 s wall vs 0.31 s inside git), so a job spends most of its wall time on process startup. Discovered while fixing deformed-cherubical-flycatcher (Gerrit 3283 removed the test-side share); this ticket removes the production share without changing what is signed or the no-push guarantee.

## Measurements

Original report (load average 30-40): `test_completion_pass_binds_server_derived_values` 60 spawns / 14.1 s; `test_completion_fail_completes_with_null_envelope` 34 spawns / 7.1 s.

Re-measured on main `90d57e392ba` (load average 32) by wrapping `subprocess.Popen.__init__` around `run_job` and recording each spawn's rebar caller: PASS job 53 spawns (49 git + 4 ssh/ssh-keygen), 4.8 s; FAIL job 32 spawns (all git), 2.8 s. Per caller, PASS job:

- `opcert_service/workspace.py:_populate` 16 + `discard` 1: init, 2 `remote add`, 2 fetch, checkout, rev-parse, 6 `git config` (3 on root, 3 repeated on the tracker worktree), `worktree add`, 2 `remote remove`; `discard` runs `worktree prune`.
- `_store/ensures.run_ensures` sweep 13 (gc/merge config probes, 4 `show`, `ls-files`). Unchanged by this ticket.
- `_engine_support/reads.py:ensure_fresh` 7: one `rev-parse --verify tickets` per ticket read (6) plus one `git fetch origin` from `_store/sync.reconverge`, which always fails because the workspace has no remote.
- Event write path 9 (`_commands/_seam.py` identity reads 3, `_store/freshness.write_blocking_divergence` 3, add, commit, `maintenance run --auto`). Unchanged.
- Signing 4 git (`_signing_manifest._gate_commit_sha` 2, `head_sha` called twice by `_opcert_signing.mint_opcert_record`) + 4 ssh. Unchanged except the duplicate `head_sha`.

## Approach

Remove only spawns that are duplicates or that cannot change the result. No ensure unit is skipped and the workspace stays a fresh, remote-less disposable clone.

1. `workspace._populate` fetches each authoritative ref by URL (`git fetch --quiet <url> <branch>`) and builds from `FETCH_HEAD` (`checkout -q -B <branch> FETCH_HEAD`, `worktree add -q -B <branch> <tracker> FETCH_HEAD`). No remote is ever configured, so the 2 `remote add` and 2 `remote remove` calls go. End state matches today's: today `remote remove` deletes `refs/remotes/*` and the branch upstream config, leaving only local branches. A throwaway probe with git 2.56 confirmed: `git remote` prints nothing and `for-each-ref` lists only `refs/heads/main` and `refs/heads/tickets`. The stall guard still applies because `_git` keys it on `args[0] == "fetch"`.
2. The repo-local identity (`user.email`, `user.name`, `commit.gpgsign=false`) is written once into the new repo's `.git/config` right after `git init`, instead of 6 `git config` processes. A linked worktree reads the shared repo config, so the 3 tracker calls were duplicates. The probe confirmed that `git -C <tracker> config user.email` returns the value written to the root config.
3. `workspace.discard` drops `git worktree prune`. The worktree registration lives under `<root>/.git/worktrees`, which the following `shutil.rmtree(root)` deletes anyway.
4. `jobs.run_job` runs the job body under the existing `rebar._engine_support.reads.local_read_context()` (the same suppression `_commands/gates.py` and `audit/read.py` use). `ensure_fresh` is the only reader of that flag (`reads.py:202`). In this remote-less clone the freshness fetch can never succeed, so it is a no-op that costs 1 + one per read. This also stops each job leaving a `/tmp/.ticket-sync-<md5>` throttle marker for its unique temp path.
5. `_opcert_signing.mint_opcert_record` resolves `head_sha` once and reuses it for both `merged_log_commit` (when the manifest has no `verified-at-sha:`) and the record's `head_sha` field. Nothing runs between the 2 calls that can move HEAD.

Expected: PASS job 53 -> 34 spawns (git 49 -> 30); FAIL job 32 -> 18.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py`: items 1-3, plus docstrings.
- `src/rebar/opcert_service/jobs.py`: item 4.
- `src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py`: item 5.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py`: new spawn-ceiling tests reusing the module's `authority`/`signer` fixtures.

## Testing

- New `test_completion_pass_spawn_ceiling` counts every `subprocess.Popen` started inside `jobs.run_job` for a completion PASS, through a test-scoped `monkeypatch` (no autouse fixture). It asserts at most 30 git and at most 34 total, and fails on main (49 git / 53 total).
- New `test_completion_fail_spawn_ceiling` asserts at most 18 for a FAIL job.
- Workspace end state: `test_server_never_pushes_and_workspace_is_isolated` already asserts no remotes and an unchanged shared store. The new PASS test also asserts that the gate sees `git for-each-ref refs/remotes` empty, and that `git config user.email` read from the tracker is `opcert@rebar.invalid`.
- Edge/failure: the existing `tests/unit/test_network_fetch_stall_abort_851e.py`, `tests/unit/test_git_timeout_bounds_77e1.py` (fetch failure and timeout become `WorkspaceError`) and `tests/unit/test_ensures_boot_budget_e43f.py` exercise the changed fetch path and must pass unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A test counts subprocess spawns inside `jobs.run_job` for a completion PASS on a test store and asserts a ceiling at least 40% below 60 (at most 34 total, at most 30 git); verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py -k spawn_ceiling` passing on the change and failing on main.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py tests/unit/test_opcert_service_integrity.py tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py` passes with no existing assertion changed (`git diff` touches no existing test body).
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_network_fetch_stall_abort_851e.py tests/unit/test_git_timeout_bounds_77e1.py tests/unit/test_ensures_boot_budget_e43f.py` passes unchanged.
- [x] The PASS and FAIL job spawn counts and `run_job` wall time, before and after, are recorded with the load average in a ticket comment.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; every `src/rebar` file stays at 800 lines or fewer and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0 increased=0`.
